messages:
maya: kicking off muon-9b bring-up. ran quick quant sweep (fp16, int8, int6) and played with prompt priming (1x vs 3x). dumping high-level notes + numbers, looking for routing/scorecard recs.
aj: pls paste the numbers.
maya: here — short table from smoke runs (synth chat workload):
```
variant | quant  | priming | p95 latency | tok/sec | delta LL
muon-9b-fp16 | fp16  | 1x      | 115ms      | 118     | baseline
muon-9b-int8 | int8  | 1x      | 98ms       | 150     | -0.02
muon-9b-int6 | int6  | 1x      | 86ms       | 178     | -0.08
muon-9b-int6 | int6  | 3x      | 102ms      | 160     | -0.03
```
maya: ballpark cost per 1k tokens (infra run-rate): fp16 ~$0.048, int8 ~$0.035, int6 ~$0.025. so int6 ~48% cheaper vs fp16.
aj: int6 latency and cost look great. quality hit of ~0.08 avgLL looks nontrivial though — any qualitative failures?
maya: yes — failure modes clustered on multi-step reasoning and entity recall after long context. short chit-chat and formatting tasks are fine. priming (3x) recovers a chunk of quality but adds prompt token overhead (roughly +2-3 tokens per priming prompt per request).
sophia: for product: we need marginal-token-payoff analysis. If priming adds 3 tokens but avoids fallback 20% of time, it might be worth it. anyone have traffic split by task length / intent?
trent: GTN asked for a scorecard we can hand to product. suggested fields: unit cost delta, p95 latency delta, %requests degraded (by severity), sample failure examples, recommended routing rule. can we produce that before EOD?
maya: I can produce a one-pager. quick draft recs:
- Default route: muon-9b-int8 (good balance).
- Fast lane: muon-9b-int6 for short-form prompts (<= 64 tokens) and retrieval-anchored completions where entity recall isn't critical.
- Safety fallback: if model confidence low or hallucination signal triggered, route to fp16 variant.
- Priming policy: use 3x short priming only on int6 when intent=="conversational" and historical pass-rate > 90%. evaluate token tax impact.
aj: can we quantify token-tax tradeoff? example: priming 3x adds ~6 tokens average per call (prompt repeating), cost delta int6 ~+6 * 0.000025 = $0.00015 per call. if that avoids a fp16 fallback (cost delta ~$0.023) 1-in-150 saves more.
sophia: product asks for thresholds: prefer int6 when expected marginal revenue per call < $0.01 and measured degradation severity low. for paid / legal flows we keep int8/fp16 pinned.
maya: ops note: int6 shows some p95 tail jitter under high batch sizes — tune batching_policy.max_batch_tokens down for int6 or reduce batch latency window.
deploy-bot: deploy check: muon-9b-int6 image passed smoke tests at 2026-03-23T14:12:00Z.
trent: ok next steps: maya to produce short scorecard (numbers + 6 sample failure traces), aj to run a 48h traffic shadow for int6 on 5% traffic, sophia to draft product routing thresholds, ops to tweak batching policy.
maya: will do. adding one more idea: run a targeted priming A/B where we compare 0x vs 3x priming on int6 for the top 10 intents by volume — that should tell us priming ROI quickly.
aj: +1. also log top 50 tokens where int6 hallucination spikes — maybe prompt-engineer can patch templates.
sophia: thanks all — this is actionable. we'll try to have scorecard + routing README by tomorrow standup. :thumbsup:
maya: attached sample failure snip below for the scorecard (sanitized):
```
user: summarize contract changes since last revision
muon-9b-int6: produced wrong party name in clause 4.2 (hallucinated "Acme Corp" instead of "Acme Innovations").
fp16: correct.
```
maya: filing the scorecard PR into repo and pinging here when ready.
trent: thanks — appreciate the fast triage.
